elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: Paragraph IV expressly states that “Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience.”

elements.element: Customer may exercise its convenience-termination right on 30 days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: Paragraph IV requires “30 days' prior” notice.

elements.element: Customer's termination notice must be written.
Licensor must provide a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees allocable to the period after termination becomes effective.
elements.evidence: Paragraph IV requires Licensor to “refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination,” which operationally provides the required pro-rata refund for the unused period.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during any committed term.
elements.evidence: Paragraph IV states that Licensor has “no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Initial Period or any extension thereof,” covering the initial and extended committed terms.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: Paragraph IV expressly grants Customer a convenience-termination right.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires 60–90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause requires 30 days' notice, not notice within the specified 60–90-day range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee may not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: Neither the original nor rendered clause imposes an early-termination fee; therefore, no fee exceeds the three-month cap.

elements.element: Vendor has a right to terminate for convenience at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause does not affirmatively grant Licensor a convenience-termination right at the end of a term.

elements.element: Vendor may not terminate for convenience before the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly denies Licensor a convenience-termination right during the Initial Period and any extension.

elements.element: Vendor's convenience termination requires 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: No 90-day notice requirement for Licensor appears in the rendered clause.

result.reason: The redline minimally adds the complete preferred protection: Customer may terminate on 30 days' written notice, receives a refund of prepaid fees for the unused period, and Licensor has no convenience-termination right during any committed term. It leaves breach termination and other unrelated provisions intact. It does not independently satisfy the fallback's exact 60–90-day Customer notice or its affirmative end-of-term, 90-day-notice Vendor termination construct.
